principles.statement: A feature being fully built is not evidence it's actually in use — check the real, currently-active configuration/default, not just whether the supporting code exists. The gap between 'this capability exists somewhere in the system' and 'this is what actually runs on a real request right now' is exactly where expensive, confusing failures hide.
principles.rationale: Confirmed live this session: every OpenRouter call failed with 402 (insufficient credits) all night, and the root cause was NOT a missing feature — the free-tier infrastructure was fully built (available_models already had a real openrouter/free entry with is_free=true, meta_fallback already had free_only=true configured) but config.toml's api_model default was still "openrouter/auto", OpenRouter's paid intelligent router. The system silently fell through to a slow-but-working BitNet fallback every time, masking the real problem as 'BitNet is just slow' rather than 'the primary config points at a paid endpoint with zero credits'.

heuristics.name: When Something Is Slow/Failing/Wrong, Check the Active Config Before the Code
heuristics.description: Before diving into code-level debugging of a system that's behaving unexpectedly (wrong routing, unexpected cost, degraded quality), read the actual currently-loaded configuration values it's running with — a correct, well-built system fed the wrong default/config value produces exactly the same symptoms as a real bug, but the fix is one line, not an investigation.
heuristics.when_to_apply: A system exhibits confusing behavior (slowness, wrong output, unexpected cost/quota consumption) and multiple subsystems (primary + fallback) could plausibly be involved.
examples: Every request 'worked' (via BitNet fallback) but was mysteriously slow — reading config.toml directly (not the code that reads it) immediately revealed api_model was still the paid auto-router, explaining the pattern in seconds instead of hours of tracing fallback logic.

heuristics.name: Multiple Independently-Built Config Files Can Silently Diverge
heuristics.description: When a project has more than one copy of the same config file (e.g. one per launch-directory convention), a fix applied to only one is a fix that appears to not work — always identify and update every real copy that could be the one actually loaded, not just the one that's easiest to find.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Fixing any config-driven bug in a project with multiple config file locations (dev vs. built-binary directories, per-environment copies, etc.).
examples: This project has config.toml at repo root AND target/release/config.toml — the server's actual CWD (target/release) determines which one loads; the fix had to be applied to both, with the CWD-relevant one explicitly noted as the one that actually matters at runtime.

decision_rules.condition: A feature that should be working (per its own code/design) appears to be failing, slow, or behaving unexpectedly, and a fallback or secondary path is quietly absorbing the failure.
decision_rules.action: Read the real, currently-active configuration directly before investigating the code paths further — verify the primary path is actually configured to use the feature that was built, not assuming it must be since the code exists.
